old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-92dv","title":"C RPL: DAO Origin Signature option (0x12) is never cryptographically verified; origin_authenticated is caller-asserted","description":"rpl_dao_process.c:226-245 validates the 0x12 DAO Origin Signature structurally only (present, exactly one, 56 bytes, final option). No DAO-domain Schnorr48 verifier exists in the C tree — lichen/subsys/lichen/link/sos_origin.c is the SOS domain (LICHEN-SOS-ORIGIN-v1), not spec/05 8.6's LICHEN-DAO-ORIGIN-v1. The test helper add_origin_signature (lichen/tests/rpl_routing/src/main.c:91-97) writes 56 dummy 0x5a bytes and the root APPLIES the DAO — pinning the absence of verification. origin_authenticated is purely caller-asserted, yet spec 05 8.6 says the root MUST verify DAO provenance, and a link-layer signature of the immediate sender does not bind the preserved DAO source to a key: an authenticated neighbor that forges the preserved source picks both origin and target and the byte-equal check passes. Fix: verify the 0x12 Schnorr48 at root ingest (schnorr48.c exists in the link subsystem — needs a DAO-domain transcript string per spec 05 8.6), or amend spec 05 8.6 to specify exactly what evidence origin_authenticated=true must represent.
